_note: PHASE 1 PLACEHOLDER SET. These 8 questions are written against the synthetic baseline corpus (data/baseline) purely to verify that the eval harness runs end to end. In Phase 2 they are REPLACED by 8 questions written from the 6 supplied fermentation cards in data/new_drop, before any search is run. Delete out/questions.lock.json (or pass --relock) when you swap them.

_schema.question: the question as asked
_schema.expected_recipe_id: recipe_id of the card that answers it - known BEFORE searching
_schema.expected_section: which part of that card holds the answer
_schema.depends_on_table_row: true when the answer is a row inside the ingredient table
_schema.answer_must_contain: strings that MUST appear in a retrieved chunk for it to count as a hit. Matching is case-insensitive and whitespace-tolerant, so '7 g' also matches '7g'. This is what makes a hit objective rather than a section-label guess.

questions.question: How much fine sea salt is in the beef bourguignon?
What is the hydration percentage of the classic rosemary focaccia?
How much amchur goes into the chana masala?
How much double cream is in the chicken tikka masala?
At what temperature and for how long is the lemon drizzle loaf baked?
How long should the pad thai rice noodles soak before they go in the wok?
What allergens does the prawn pad thai contain?
What is the rice to water ratio for the ginger and spring onion congee?

generation_unanswerable: What is the calorie and macronutrient breakdown per serving of the beef bourguignon?
How many milligrams of sodium are in one portion of the chana masala?
Which wine does the archive recommend pairing with the chicken tikka masala?

bonus.question: When does the fine sea salt go into the beef bourguignon, and how much is it?
bonus.note: This is the precision/completeness probe. The tight ingredient-row chunk answers 'how much' precisely and carries no method prose about *when*; the looser baseline window may drag in surrounding method text and answer the timing half.
